check_geometric_continuity.py_change.mechanism: Directly reproduced the concrete effect: of the 9,176 known junction_connector_issues (Fix 1's territory), 581 involve a road <= 1.0m; of those, 481 do NOT fit the general ~3.5m-multiple lane-offset signature that explains 94% of the broader population. Characterized those 481 precisely: dxy is 0.0000m at the median (position exactly matches its neighbour) while dhdg clusters near pi (up to exactly 180.00 degrees) -- a clean, narrow signature distinct from genuine discontinuities, consistent with a sub-meter/sub-decimeter road's own heading being underdetermined or convention-mismatched, not a real defect.
check_geometric_continuity.py_change.implementation: When a flagged link has dxy <= eps_xy (position already fine) AND either connected road is a micro-stub AND dhdg > eps_hdg, the record is now routed to a new 'micro_stub_heading_advisory' bucket instead of 'issues'/'junction_connector_issues' -- mirroring this function's own existing 'diagnostic evidence, not a hard failure' treatment already used for junction_connector_issues. Genuine ~3.5m-multiple lane-offset issues that happen to involve a micro-stub road are NOT reclassified (only 100/581 fit that pattern and are left exactly where they were).
